findings.finding: Compilation now requires exact blueprint bytes, exact prior receipt bytes, the sealed intent, both source object digests, both source file digests, and one grounded-consent subject binding the complete packet. Object and file digests remain separate.

The subject, compiler profile, acceptance matrix, receipt, generated schemas, and runtime normalizers close object records and reject version drift, extra fields, forged truth, artifact substitution, and inconsistent resource observations.
Every routed acceptance verdict is fixed at UNRUN. Composer validation is retained only as source status, and desired semantic outcomes require human review.

The first adversarial run showed that a lower-case Windows drive alias passed the inherited root guard. The compiler now requires upper-case canonical drive spelling before validating one new direct-child root.
Exact input bytes, exact output bytes, file count, and single-attempt scope are enforced. Duration and memory remain declared but not independently enforced or measured.

Generated schemas express only the blueprint's declared JSON types and closed object boundary. No independent third-party schema validator, semantic implementation, runtime behavior, quality, or performance proof is present.
No future generated code may be copied for direct reuse until Mike decides its source rights are sufficient. This run emits no code.
A future repaired executor remains unauthorized. No supplied experimental runtime or candidate executor was run.
